given: a Property with rooms, beds, bookings and Stays
when: a Staff Member opens the calendar
then: one row per room with its beds beneath it, and every booking and Stay drawn as a bar on the Unit it names

situation: CONCURRENCY — a check-in lands during the read
given: a confirmed Reservation being checked in by another Staff Member
when: the calendar is read at the same moment
then: the Guest is drawn exactly once — as confirmed or as in house, never both and never neither — because Units and bars come from one statement

given: bars ending on the first day, ending on the second, starting on the last day and starting the day after the window
then: the first and the last are not drawn; the two in between are. Nights are daterange(starts_on, ends_on, '[)') on both sides

situation: TIME — today is the Property's day
given: Properties in Pacific/Kiritimati (UTC+14) and Pacific/Pago_Pago (UTC−11)
then: today and the default window follow app.property_today for that Property, not the server's or the reader's calendar

given: no start date and no length in the request
then: the window starts three days before the Property's today and runs 14 days

given: a request for 7, 14, 30, 0, 365 or a word
then: 7, 14 and 30 are honoured; anything else reads 14 days. The read is never unbounded

situation: A start date that is not a date
given: a start of 2026-02-30 or free text
then: the default window is read instead; nothing is refused and no error reaches the screen

given: a start date five years back or ahead
then: the window is read like any other — there is no range limit on where it starts, only on its length

situation: TIME — midnight passes while it is open
given: the calendar showing the default window
when: the Property's day rolls and the next refresh arrives
then: today's column moves and a Stay due yesterday becomes overdue. A window with an explicit start in the URL stays where it is

given: a confirmed Reservation made with createReservation
then: it is drawn over its planned nights, solid, labelled with the Guest's name

given: a requested Reservation (no command creates one on main; the test inserts it)
then: it is drawn dashed and labelled Requested. It holds no night: the nightly free count does not drop for it, and Show requested can hide it

given: a confirmed Reservation checked in with checkIn
then: one bar, the Stay's, carrying the Reservation's id. The Reservation's own checked_in status draws nothing

given: a Reservation for the 5th to the 8th checked in on the 6th
when: the calendar is read and the bar opened
then: the bar starts on the 6th; the drawer shows booked 5–8 and arrived 6

given: a Stay withdrawn with reverseCheckIn, its Reservation confirmed again
then: the withdrawn Stay is not drawn and the Reservation is drawn again over its planned nights

given: a Stay in house whose ends_on is before today
then: the bar runs through tonight, not to the planned end, and says Overdue with the date it was due. The Guest is in the Unit

given: a Stay in house whose ends_on is today
then: it is not overdue and its bar ends today

given: a Stay in house with ends_on null that began before the window
then: the bar enters from the window's start edge and runs off its end, labelled No end date. It never ends tomorrow for want of a date

given: a Stay checked out with checkOut inside the window
then: it is drawn muted over the nights actually stayed, and Show departed can hide it

situation: TIME — checked out on the day of arrival
given: a Stay whose starts_on equals its ends_on
then: nothing is drawn: the range [d,d) holds no night

given: a Stay for the 5th to the 10th checked out on the 7th
then: the departed bar covers the 5th and 6th, and the nights from the 7th count as free

given: a Reservation cancelled with cancelReservation, one marked no-show with markNoShow, and a cancelled Stay
then: none of them is drawn and none holds a night

given: an in-house Stay with no reservation_id (inserted by the test; no command creates one on main)
then: it is drawn, and its label and drawer say No Guest recorded

given: a Stay in status reserved (nothing creates one)
then: it is not drawn. Its Reservation already is, and drawing both would show one booking twice

given: an overdue Stay with no charges
then: the Stay is not drawn and the Reservation is drawn again over its planned nights, now in the past

given: an overdue Stay
when: it is checked out with checkOut
then: the departed bar ends today, the day they left, not on the day they were due

given: a Property with rooms let whole, rooms let by the bed, and a bed with no room
then: each night counts the sellable Units — Units with no children — that no confirmed, in-house, overdue or departed bar holds and that are not blocked or out of service from today on. A room with beds is never counted; its beds are

given: a Guest in house on a Unit
when: a Reservation over one of their remaining nights is created with createReservation, or already exists from before #60
then: the new booking is refused by unit_holds_one_occupancy (since #60) and the calendar shows one bar; a row written before that trigger is drawn as two bars, stacked, each keeping its own state's icon and marked with the Overlap icon and — where the bar is wide enough to read it — the word, which is always in its accessible name and its drawer; and the Property's overlap count is one

situation: TIME — overdue into a booked night
given: a Guest leaving today and a confirmed Reservation from today on the same Unit — a changeover, which the database allows
when: the Property's day moves on with the Guest still in house
then: the Guest is overdue and held through tonight, which is the booking's first night: the two overlap and are counted. The day passing writes nothing a trigger could refuse, so this is how an overlap still arises

given: one bar ending on the 8th and the next starting on the 8th on the same Unit
then: no overlap: they share the 8th's cell, one ending at its middle and the other starting there

given: the named gap on a Unit, or an overdue Guest holding a booked night (RC-S1-26)
when: the in-house Guest is checked out with checkOut, or the booking is cancelled with cancelReservation
then: the next read shows no overlap and a count of zero. A departed Stay still covers the nights it held, the booked one included when the Guest overstayed, but it collides with nothing: those nights are history, and unit_holds_one_occupancy does not count a departed Stay either

given: a requested Reservation over a confirmed or in-house bar
then: both are drawn and the requested one is marked as clashing; its drawer says confirming it as it stands would be refused — by reservations_no_double_booking over a confirmed booking, by unit_holds_one_occupancy over a Guest in house. A departed Stay is history and clashes with nothing. It is not counted as an overlap: it holds nothing yet

given: an in-house Stay, a confirmed and a requested Reservation on one Unit's night
then: three lanes in that row, one overlap counted, and lanes reused by later bars that do not collide

situation: The count ignores what is hidden
given: an overlap on floor 3 and the view filtered to floor 1, or searched for another Guest
then: the count still reads one, and choosing it shows only the Units with an overlap

given: a Unit blocked with blockUnit and a reason
then: its label shows a lock and Blocked; its cells from today on are hatched with the reason; past cells are left clear because a block has no start date

given: a blocked Unit
then: the next read draws it free from today

given: a confirmed Reservation on a Unit blocked afterwards (allowed, RB-S3-05; its check-in will be refused, RB-S3-06)
then: the bar is drawn over the hatch and counted apart from overlaps as booked while blocked

situation: REVERSAL — booked while blocked is cleared
given: a booking on a blocked Unit
when: the Unit is unblocked, or the booking cancelled
then: the next read no longer counts it

given: a Unit whose status is out_of_service (no command writes it on main; the test sets it)
then: it is drawn like a block, labelled Out of order — the word Maintenance and Arrivals use — with the reference of the request that holds it, and the day it is back in its tooltip and in the details of a booking over it (MAINT-12, MAINT-17)

given: a bed Unit with no parent — the dormitory case
then: it is its own row, sellable, at the level of rooms

given: rooms named 2, 10 and 101 on one floor
then: they appear 2, 10, 101, not 10, 101, 2

given: Units in two buildings, on several floors, some with no floor and some with no building
then: grouped by building then floor; no floor goes last under No floor; Units with no building go last under No building when others have one, and with no buildings at all there is no building heading

given: a room let by the bed with four beds
then: one row remains showing beds taken on each night, 3/4; expanding shows each bed again. Collapse all and Expand all act on every room

given: a Guest staying inside the window and one staying outside it
when: a Staff Member searches by name or room number
then: only matching rooms remain; the Guest outside the window is not found, and the empty result says No rooms match with Clear filters

situation: ACCESS — a Property out of reach
given: a Staff Member with no assignment to the Property
when: the calendar is read for it
then: no Units and no bars — the same answer as an empty Property, not an error

given: the front_desk capability off, the Entitlement lost, or the Subscription lapsed
then: no Units; the page shows the no-front-desk state and the rail has no Room calendar

given: a Property of an Organization the Staff Member does not belong to
then: nothing is returned

given: a Staff Member reaching two Properties
then: only that Property's Units and bars come back. The policy admits both; the predicate picks one, and deleting it must fail this test

given: a Resident signed in to the Portal
when: the calendar read or route is asked for
then: nothing is returned; the Resident's own Stay policies never reach another Unit (ADR 0009)

given: no session
when: the calendar's refresh route is called
then: 401 with no body

given: an in-house or departed Stay with a Folio carrying lines
then: the drawer shows the sum of the Folio's lines in the Folio's currency, as Departures does, and says Closed when the Folio is

given: a Reservation not yet checked in, or a Stay with no Folio
then: no balance line at all — never a zero that looks like a settled account

given: a Property with no Units
then: No rooms yet, with a link to Rooms & beds

given: Units but no bars in the window
then: the grid is drawn with every night free and a line saying nothing is booked between the window's first and last day

given: a window on screen
when: previous, next, today, a date or a length is chosen
then: the old grid stays until the new one arrives, marked as updating; nothing blanks. A window that cannot be read is put back — URL and toolbar with it — and the screen says so, with the time of the calendar still shown

given: the calendar open and the refresh route failing
then: the last grid stays with Couldn't refresh and the time of the data shown; the route logs the failure with the Property and viewer ids and no Guest data

given: a render error in the calendar
then: a boundary for the page shows a retry instead of a blank workspace, and the error is logged

given: the locale ar
then: days run right to left, bars and their half-day ends mirror, and the drawer opens from the left

given: tr, en and ar
then: every string exists in all three; nights and overlap counts use ICU plurals including Arabic's categories; calendar days are formatted without shifting a day

given: a screen too narrow for the window
then: the days scroll sideways while the room column stays pinned

given: a keyboard user
then: the bar is a button named with the Guest, dates and status; Enter opens the drawer; Escape closes it and returns focus to the bar

given: every bar state, overlap, block and booked-while-blocked
then: each carries a word or an icon with a label, not only a colour

given: a view with a start, length, floor, toggles, search and collapsed rooms
then: the same view opens; any parameter that is not valid is ignored on its own without discarding the rest

given: the length and the two toggles chosen in this browser (there is no grouping to choose, and folded rooms are per room, so they belong in the URL)
when: the calendar is opened again without parameters
then: it opens with them; the start date and search are not remembered, and anything in the URL wins

given: the calendar open and a Guest checked in on Arrivals
when: 30 seconds pass with the tab visible
then: the bar changes to in house; with the tab hidden the refresh waits

situation: ACCESS — a switch is never answered from cache
given: a Staff Member who switches Property, or a second person signing in on the same browser
then: nothing from the previous Property or person appears — the cache key is the user, the Organization and the Property (ADR 0019)

given: a confirmed booking arriving today, an in-house Stay, and any other bar
then: links go to Arrivals, Departures and Reservations respectively, each keeping the Property

given: a bar's drawer open
when: the booking is cancelled or checked out elsewhere and the refresh arrives
then: the drawer says the booking has changed and shows its new state, or that it is no longer on the calendar

given: a Stay from the 5th to the 8th
then: the bar starts at the middle of the 5th and ends at the middle of the 8th

given: an Organization default of 30 days with beds shown
when: any of its Properties without an override is opened
then: the calendar opens with 30 days and beds shown

given: an Organization default of 14 days and a Property override of 30
when: that Property is opened, then its override is reset
then: it opens at 30, then at 14. Reset clears the value; the row is never deleted

given: a URL parameter, a remembered browser choice, a Property override and an Organization default all set
then: URL, then browser, then Property, then Organization, then the built-in 14 days from three days before today

given: a Staff Member without accommodation.configure
when: they try to set a default
then: refused. accommodation.configure is the permission PR #57's inspection setting uses, so one permission governs a Property's configuration

given: a Staff Member of one Organization
when: they try to set a default for another's Property
then: refused by the policy, whatever the permission

given: two Staff Members saving a Property's default together
then: one row remains for that Property and the later save is the value

given: a default length of 60 days
then: refused by the database: only 7, 14 and 30

given: a default changed
then: an audit record says who changed which default from what to what

situation: Drag a booking to another Unit or other days
given: a confirmed or requested booking that has not arrived, and a Staff Member holding front_desk.amend
when: its bar is dragged to another row, or along its row, and released
then: nothing is written by the drop. The Change booking dialog opens on the Unit and nights dropped on, showing From → To (Unit, dates, nights), the price the dialog already shows, and whether the move is allowed. Confirming saves through the existing command (app.amend_reservation); cancelling leaves the booking where it was. Dropped where it started, nothing opens

given: a bar being dragged over a row
then: a dashed outline shows the nights the bar would take on the row under the pointer, and is marked with an icon, not colour alone, when the calendar already knows it cannot go there. The bar left behind is drawn faint

situation: TIME — nights are half-open, so a departure day is free for an arrival
given: a Unit with one booking leaving on the 8th and another arriving on the 12th
when: a booking is dropped to arrive on the 8th and leave on the 12th, and to arrive on the 7th
then: the first shows no conflict, because nights are [arrival, departure); the second names the booking whose night it shares. The same boundary decides for a Guest in house moving rooms and for a stay extended up to the next arrival

situation: A conflict is shown before the move, and the move cannot be confirmed
given: a drop on a Unit that another confirmed booking or a Guest in house holds for some of the nights
then: it names the booking's Guest, or the Guest staying, in words, and the confirm button is disabled. The database's own answer for the same nights is shown only when the calendar did not already say it. Nothing has changed

situation: A Unit that cannot take a booking
given: a Unit blocked or out of service from today on, and a room let by the bed
when: a booking or a Guest is dropped on either
then: the preview says the Unit is blocked or out of service for some of those nights, or that the room is let by the bed and one of its beds should be chosen, and cannot be confirmed. A block has no dates, so nights wholly before today are not its

situation: TIME — a past day, a stay that ended, a bar no command can change
given: a booking dropped to arrive before today, and a departed Stay or a Stay with no booking dragged anywhere
then: the first says the arrival must be today or later; the others open a preview that says the stay cannot be moved and has nothing to confirm. A Stay is changed only through its booking, so nothing is offered for one without

situation: A Guest in house dragged to another room
given: a Guest in house and a Staff Member holding front_desk.amend
when: their bar is dragged to another row
then: the Move Guest dialog opens on that Unit and asks for the reason the command requires (ADR 0039); confirming moves them from tonight through app.move_stay. Dragging across days changes nothing: they keep the day they arrived. The nights already slept stay drawn in the room they left

situation: A Guest in house, the end of their stay pulled
given: a Guest in house whose bar ends on the grid
when: the grip at the end of the bar is pulled to another day
then: the Change departure dialog opens on that day, showing From → To and the extra nights' price; a booking that holds a night it would add blocks it in words, and leaving today or earlier is told as a check-out. Confirming saves through app.change_departure

situation: CONCURRENCY — the room is taken while the preview is open
given: a preview with nothing in the way, and another Staff Member who books the Unit before it is confirmed
then: the command refuses, the dialog says in words that the Unit is already booked and keeps nothing, and closing it reads the calendar again so the booking that won is drawn. The same holds for a stale version and a Unit no longer in service: the database decides

given: a Staff Member who reaches the calendar without front_desk.amend
then: bars have no grab cursor, no hint, no end grip and no Move…, and a pointer drag hands nothing on. The commands refuse such a caller as well (ADR 0039); this only stops the screen offering what would be refused

situation: Arabic — the drag runs the right way
given: the locale ar
when: a booking is dragged to a later day
then: the pointer travels to the left, the dates in the preview are the right ones, and the dialog is laid out from the right. Days are found from what is drawn under the pointer, so no arithmetic of a direction exists to get wrong

situation: Keyboard and screen reader — Move… without a pointer
given: a booking that has not arrived, opened from its bar, and a Staff Member holding front_desk.amend
when: Move… is pressed in the drawer
then: the same preview opens on where the booking is, with the date and Unit pickers, and nothing to save until something changes. A Guest in house has Move Guest and Change departure in the same drawer

situation: A touch screen scrolls instead of dragging
given: a finger on a bar
then: the grid scrolls, as a swipe over a bar should, and nothing is dragged. A booking is moved from its details with Move…

situation: Filters by Unit type and by state
given: a Property with rooms and suites, some blocked
when: a Unit type or a Unit state is chosen
then: only Units of that type or in that state remain, a room staying with its beds when one of them is what was asked for. Only the types and states the Property has are offered. They are in the link, any value that is not a type or a state is dropped on its own, and the counts above the grid still cover every Unit

given: a booking whose bar ends on the grid
when: the grip at the end of the bar is pulled to another day
then: the Change booking dialog opens on the new departure with the same preview; the arrival and the Unit are unchanged, and the booking keeps at least one night. Its start is not pulled (RC-DEF-10)

situation: Escape, and a click that is not a drag
given: a bar pressed
when: the pointer travels and Escape is pressed, or the pointer does not travel
then: Escape drops the drag: the outline goes, nothing opens, nothing changes. A press that does not travel is a click and opens the drawer, and the click a finished drag leaves behind does not

situation: The calendar and the commands agree
given: bookings dropped on Units free, booked, occupied, out of service, let by the bed, and on days past
when: each drop is checked by the calendar and then saved
then: where the calendar names a conflict the command refuses, with the outcome the dialog words; where it names none the command accepts. The same holds for a Guest moved and a departure pulled. They are two statements of one rule and only a run of both can say they match

given: the Organization-default and Property-override settings shape exists only on feat/housekeeping-inspection
then: resolved: PR #57 merged the Organization-default and Property-override settings shape. Slice 2 is unblocked and not started

given: ADR 0021 is not applied on main: app.property_today is the calendar day in the Property's time zone
when: the calendar marks today between midnight and the cutoff
then: resolved by #60, which applied ADR 0021: app.property_today is now the business date (local time less the Property's cutoff, 04:00 by default). The calendar reads nothing else, so it followed with no change to its read, and the subtitle now says business days

given: a URL naming a Property the Staff Member cannot use
then: resolved by #63: frontDeskProperty now answers a ?property= the viewer cannot use with the empty state rather than the first entitled Property (HK-S1-24), so the calendar never draws one Property's rooms under a switcher naming another. Unknown, out of reach and switched off still look alike

given: a requested Reservation
then: its bar turns solid and holds its nights. No command confirms a request on main

given: a Guest with no booking
then: an in-house bar with no Reservation. No command creates a walk-in on main; RC-S1-22 draws one inserted by a test

given: a departed Stay
then: the bar returns to in house. reverseCheckOut is check-out slice 3 and not built

given: a requested or confirmed Reservation
when: it is cancelled or marked no-show
then: resolved by #60: cancelReservation and markNoShow exist, and RC-S1-21 now uses them. The bar goes and its nights are free

given: feat/front-desk-occupancy adds the Reservation status checked_out
then: resolved by #60 bringing checked_out to main: the Reservation predicate is an allow-list of requested and confirmed, so a checked-out Guest is drawn once, through the departed Stay, and not at all when they left the day they came

given: a front-desk arrangement used every morning
then: deferred: blueprint 18.6 names saved views; they need a table per person and nobody has asked for one yet

given: planned work on a Unit next week
when: it is put on the calendar
then: deferred to Maintenance (RANZ-33), which holds out-of-order Units with an optional expected-back date. Once merged the hatch ends at that date, and a Guest in house on an out-of-order Unit counts as booked while blocked

given: an arriving Guest's bar opened
when: the Staff Member wants to check them in there
then: deferred: each command keeps one home for now (Arrivals, Departures, Reservations); blueprint 18.6's action cluster comes later

situation: Move, extend or shorten by dragging
given: a bar dragged to another Unit or date
then: superseded by RC-S3-01 to RC-S3-17: the reason it waited has gone, because the commands of ADR 0039 now move a booking and a Guest, each checking its caller and refusing a conflict, so a drag proposes and those commands decide. What is still deferred is RC-DEF-10 to RC-DEF-12

given: a hotel that sorts by Deluxe, Twin and Suite
then: deferred: a price is per unit type (ADR 0038), not per room category, so Units still have no category to group by

given: a Staff Member whose work is not the front desk
then: deferred: names are shown to anyone with reach and front_desk, as Arrivals and Departures show them. A role-based read of Guest names is a decision for every front-desk read at once

given: a residence planning a term
then: deferred: the allowed lengths are one constant; a longer view needs narrower cells without names and is added when asked for

given: the workspace has no error reporter and no route-level boundary today
when: a calendar error happens in the browser
then: deferred for the workspace as a whole: this feature adds its own page boundary and server-side logging (RC-S1-53, RC-S1-54); where client errors are sent is a decision for every screen

given: a booking whose bar begins on the grid
then: deferred: the arrival is moved with the whole bar (RC-S3-01) or in Move…; a grip on the start is another handle to place and test, and nobody has asked for it

given: a touch screen
then: deferred: a finger on a bar is a swipe over the grid (RC-S3-13); a long press to pick a bar up is the usual answer and is a design of its own

situation: Drag past the edge of the window
given: a booking dragged towards a day outside the window shown
then: deferred: the grid does not scroll itself while dragging, so a move beyond the window is made with Move… or after paging; automatic scrolling is a behaviour to tune with real use

given: a Reservation asked for over an in-house Stay's remaining nights
then: resolved by #60: unit_holds_one_occupancy refuses a booking over a Guest in house for every role, so the named gap is closed at write time. The calendar still marks an overlap that arises by the day passing (RC-S1-26) or from rows written before #60 (RC-S1-25)

situation: An overdue Guest is in the room tonight
given: a Guest in house ten days past their planned departure, with a Folio that has been charged nothing since
when: their bar and their details are read
then: the bar's accessible name says they are in house, overdue, arrived on a date, due on another and still in the room tonight; the details say how many days late, the nights counted through tonight, and label the balance as of the last charge with a note that later nights post at the close of the day or at check-out; Change departure is offered, as for any Guest in house
test_name: room-calendar-ux.spec.ts: an overdue Guest's bar and details say they are still in the room tonight

situation: The days can be told apart
given: a window of seven, fourteen or thirty days in Turkish, English or Arabic
then: each heading is the language's short weekday and the date, so no two days of a week share a letter (Arabic narrows only at thirty days, where its seven letters are all different); the first column and every 1st carry their month; Saturdays and Sundays are tinted, and today keeps its own tint
test_name: room-calendar-ux.spec.ts: the day headings tell the days apart, mark the month, and tint the weekend

situation: A short bar names its Guest at once
given: a one-night booking, too narrow to hold its Guest's name
when: it is pointed at with a mouse or reached by keyboard
then: a card with the Guest, the state and the dates appears at once, with no wait for the browser's own tooltip; a name keeps its own direction, so a Latin name in an Arabic row is cut at its end, not its front
test_name: room-calendar-ux.spec.ts: a one-night booking names its Guest at once, on hover and on focus

situation: The grid is one tab stop
given: a calendar with forty bars
when: a keyboard user tabs through the page
then: one bar is in the tab order, and the arrow keys move to the bar beside, above or below it and Home and End to the ends of the row, so the first booking is not the fortieth stop on the page; Enter still opens the drawer (RC-S1-58)
test_name: room-calendar-ux.spec.ts: the bars are one tab stop, and the arrow keys move between them

situation: A phone has room for the grid
given: a viewport below md
then: the second heading and the description are gone, the room column is a phone's share of the width, and the six filters and the legend are folded behind one button and one disclosure that says how many filters narrow the grid, so the grid starts a third of the way down the first screen
test_name: room-calendar-ux.spec.ts: on a phone the filters and the legend fold away, and the grid starts high up

situation: The toolbar says what it does
given: the toolbar at any width
then: the arrows say they step seven days; the two toggles say they show requested and departed Guests, in the words the legend uses, on one line; the date jumped to is marked in its column until another move; and a window with nothing booked says so under the grid, so the grid does not jump while paging
test_name: room-calendar-ux.spec.ts: the toolbar names its steps, keeps its two toggles on one line, and marks the date jumped to

situation: A window that does not fit says so
given: a window wider than the screen, and fourteen days on a laptop with the sidebar open
then: fourteen days fit without scrolling; a window that does not fit shows a fade at its far edge until it is scrolled to the end
test_name: room-calendar-ux.spec.ts: a 30-day window that does not fit shows a cue at its edge, until it is scrolled to the end

situation: The details carry what the desk asks
given: a booking arriving today into a dirty room, and a Guest booked as a Resident
then: the details give the reservation code, say whether the room is ready, dirty, waiting for inspection or occupied (for a booking that has begun, never for one days away), name the stay type only for a Resident, and keep the actions a space apart from the facts
test_name: room-calendar-ux.spec.ts: a booking's details give its code and whether its room is ready, and no meaningless type

situation: Focus goes back to what was pressed
given: the details open over the calendar and a dialog opened from them (Move guest, Change departure, Move)
then: focus returns to the button that opened it, with the details still open under it, and not to the page
test_name: room-calendar-ux.spec.ts: closing a dialog opened from the details puts focus back on the button that opened it

situation: A Stay's bar names its booking
given: a Guest in house on a booking
then: the Stay's bar carries the booking's reference, so the drawer can name the booking as the Move dialog does; null for a Stay that began without one (ROOMCAL-09)

situation: A move dialog names the proposed room while it loads
given: a booking moved from the calendar, with the dialog's rooms still loading
then: the Unit field and the summary name the proposed room, never an id or a dash, and the Stay's bar details give the booking's code (ROOMCAL-05, ROOMCAL-09)
